rationales.wacc: 10.5% (analyst judgment). AMD's capital structure is almost all equity: long-term debt $7.1B (balance sheet, 2026-09-26) against a market capitalisation of roughly $790B (last close $483.90 on 2026-11-03 x 1,640M cover-page shares), so WACC is roughly the cost of equity. Cost of equity assumes a risk-free rate of about 4.25%, an equity risk premium of about 5% and a beta of about 1.25 for a high-beta, cyclical semiconductor designer with concentrated customers (periodic.txt notes a small number of customers account for a substantial part of revenue) and export-control exposure (Q-6). That gives about 10.5%. The cost of debt is not material at this weight. The risk-free rate, ERP and beta are not in the snapshot; they are assumptions, not sourced facts.
rationales.terminal_growth: 3.0% (analyst judgment): roughly long-run nominal GDP plus a modest premium for semiconductor content growth (AI/data-center compute). It stays well below the 10.5% WACC and does not assume the current AI-driven growth continues forever.
rationales.revenue_growth: Year 1 is the code's NTM revenue from assumptions.json (about $72.6B, anchored on the $17.0B FY2026Q4 guidance midpoint, Q-1). That is already about 60% above TTM revenue of $45.4B (FY2025Q4 $10.27B + FY2026Q1-Q3 $35.17B; F-da2eaa33df less F-24d3538948, plus F-80df404447). Years 2-5 slow down: 25%, 18%, 12%, 8%. The data-center/rack-scale ramp (Q-3, Q-4) supports strong growth after year 1, but a base this large, lumpy system shipments and export-control risk (Q-6) argue for a glide path towards the terminal rate rather than a straight extrapolation of the FY2026 trend. These rates are analyst judgment. Customer-warrant contra-revenue (Q-15, $4.5B unrecognized) is not separately deducted from years 2-5. It is non-cash, and its economic cost is taken as share dilution (see customer_warrants), so it is not double counted.
rationales.peers: NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, INTC: the coverage-list names whose business is closest to AMD's. NVDA competes directly in data-center GPUs/accelerators. AVGO and MRVL sell data-center compute and networking silicon (custom accelerators) to the same hyperscale customers. INTC competes directly with AMD in x86 client and server CPUs, AMD's other large franchise. Excluded: MU (commodity memory with a different margin cycle); AMAT, LRCX and KLAC (wafer-fab equipment, a capex-cycle business model); SNPS and CDNS (EDA software); ALAB and CRDO (small-cap connectivity names with TTM revenue near $1.6B, where scale and growth profile are not comparable); MPWR (power management). Including INTC (a low EV/Sales name) alongside the AI-premium names keeps the median representative of AMD's mixed CPU-plus-accelerator portfolio. Pre-check of TTM EV/Sales from the snapshot: NVDA ~16.5x, AVGO ~18.2x, MRVL ~16.1x, INTC ~5.8x; code computes the final median. TTM period alignment (dates verified in snapshot/peers.json, latest revenue facts accepted before the cutoff): AMD's TTM ends 2026-09-26 (FY2026Q3 10-Q). INTC's TTM also ends 2026-09-26 (Q3 10-Q accepted 2026-10-29), so it is aligned. The other three peers report on non-calendar fiscal years and their latest filed quarter ends earlier: NVDA 2026-07-26 (about two months before AMD's TTM end), AVGO 2026-08-02 (about eight weeks earlier) and MRVL 2026-08-01 (about eight weeks earlier). Their next quarters were not filed by the cutoff, so code uses these lagged TTMs. Bias: all three lagged peers are growing fast (from the same filings, NVDA quarterly revenue rose from about $81.6B to $96.2B, and MRVL from about $2.42B to $2.74B, quarter on quarter). A TTM that ends about two months earlier therefore understates their current revenue run rate, and EV/Sales on that TTM is modestly overstated. The two middle values that set the median (NVDA and MRVL) are both lagged, so the median multiple, and with it the peer EV/Sales leg, is biased upward. My rough estimate, an analyst judgment rather than a computed figure, is several percent up to about 10%. I do not adjust the multiple for this: code applies a mechanical median to the latest filed TTM. The bias is disclosed here, and it should be read as making the relative leg a generous cross-check.
rationales.fcf_margin: Historical FCF margin = (CFO - capex) / revenue, all from snapshot XBRL facts. FY2022 13.2% ((3,565-450)/23,601); FY2023 4.9% ((1,667-546)/22,680); FY2024 9.3% ((3,041-636)/25,785); FY2025 19.4% ((7,709-974)/34,639; F-ba5e841822, F-9407f71787, F-da2eaa33df); 9M FY2026 13.3% ((6,523-1,845)/35,166; F-453f71f069, F-15168cdccc, F-80df404447); TTM to 2026-09-26 15.5% ((7,056)/45,436). Quarterly FY2026 runs 25.0%, 13.5%, 4.1% (Q1-Q3). The decline reflects a working-capital build (inventories $7.9B to $11.5B, receivables $6.3B to $9.2B since 2025-12-27) and capex up to about 5% of revenue. Year 1 at 18% sits between TTM (15.5%) and the FY2025 peak (19.4%): the model's GAAP operating margin of about 25-26% (assumptions.json gross margin ~53.5% less opex ~28%) supports more than TTM, but 60% revenue growth will keep absorbing working capital. Margins rise to 20%, 21% and 22% as growth slows, working-capital drag eases and fixed intangible amortization/opex shrink relative to revenue, then hold at 22%. That is still below the after-tax operating margin plus non-cash add-backs, as a haircut for capex intensity and because CFO includes the SBC add-back (SBC ~4.3% of 9M FY2026 revenue, F-c00e259756), which is a real economic cost.
rationales.dcf_weight: 0.6 DCF / 0.4 peer EV/Sales. The DCF carries more weight because it rests on this note's explicit, sourced forecasts (guidance-anchored NTM revenue, history-grounded FCF margins). The peer EV/Sales cross-check is applied to AMD's TTM revenue. It gets real weight because it captures the market's sector-wide pricing of AI-compute growth beyond our five-year horizon, which a fixed-margin DCF may understate. It does not get a majority because those multiples embed peer-specific growth and margin profiles (NVDA's much higher margins, INTC's restructuring) and current sentiment rather than AMD's cash flows. Both legs are divided by the same 1,661M diluted shares, which exclude up to 320M contingently issuable customer warrant shares (see customer_warrants). Full vesting would cut both legs, and so the blended target, by about 16% (to about $249 from $297; our arithmetic). The rating band would be unchanged, so the weight itself is unaffected.
rationales.customer_warrants: Potential dilution not in the code's share count. AMD issued warrants to two customers (October 2025, February 2026), 'each entitling the holder the right to purchase up to 160 million shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share' (Q-12), 'up to a combined 320 million shares' (Q-18). As of 2026-09-26 'no warrant shares had vested or become exercisable' (Q-16), and the shares are 'considered contingently issuable and are excluded from the computation of basic and diluted earnings per share' until vested and exercisable (Q-17). So the code's diluted share count of 1,661M (F-15b3d74691, computed/valuation.json diluted_shares) contains none of the warrant shares. Full vesting would add up to 320M shares, about 19.3% of 1,661M (our arithmetic). Direction and size (our arithmetic from round-003 computed/valuation.json, not a code output): this is an upper bound that assumes full vesting of both warrants and ignores the $0.01 exercise proceeds (about $3.2M in total, negligible). Using 1,661M + 320M = 1,981M shares: DCF leg = equity value $324.5B / 1,981M = about $163.8 per share (code: $195.37). Relative leg = $748.0B equity ($450.35 x 1,661M) / 1,981M = about $377.6 (code: $450.35). Blend at dcf_weight 0.6 = about $249.3 (code: $297.36, target price $297). That is a cut of about 16.2% in the target, because each per-share value scales by 1,661/1,981 = 0.838. Implied upside against the $483.90 close (2026-11-03) would be about -48.5% instead of -38.6%. The direction is down. Under the policy bands (Underperform <= -10% upside) the rating stays Underperform; dilution only moves the target further below the price. Why this is a disclosed sensitivity rather than an input: the code divides by reported diluted shares and has no contingent-share input. Vesting depends on customer purchase milestones and other conditions with no timing in the filing. Partial or no vesting is possible, so 320M is the ceiling, not an expected value. The DCF does capitalise the same Data Center/rack-scale ramp (Q-3, Q-4) that would drive vesting, so the full-dilution figure should be read as the relevant downside case if that ramp is delivered. gen-model's share_change_qoq deliberately excludes the warrants and defers them to this sensitivity (assumptions.json). Contra-revenue (Q-15): the $4.5B of unrecognized grant-date fair value 'would be recorded as a reduction of revenue proportionally as qualifying customer revenue is recognized'. It will therefore lower future reported revenue. FY2026Q4 is anchored on GAAP revenue guidance (Q-1), which we judge to be net of any Q4 contra-revenue, although the release does not say so. Our year 2-5 growth rates and FCF margins are not separately reduced for it. That is deliberate: the reduction is non-cash, because the consideration paid to the customer is shares, not cash. It lowers reported revenue, and so reported FCF margin on a reported-revenue base, but not cash flow. Its economic cost is the share dilution above. Cutting forecast cash flow as well as applying the dilution would count the same cost twice. On a reported basis, revenue in the years when tranches are earned could be up to $4.5B lower in total than gross customer billings, with FCF unchanged, so reported FCF margins would be slightly higher than modelled. Warrant liability (Q-14): the $1.2B warrant liability (in other long-term liabilities) is excluded from net cash. The warrants are 'not settleable in cash' (Q-13). Under the accounting policy (periodic.txt) the liability is remeasured until each tranche becomes exercisable, 'at which point the related liability is reclassified to Additional paid-in capital'. It will never require a cash outflow, so it is not debt-like. Its economic cost is the dilution sensitivity above. Deducting it from net cash as well would double count.
rationales.net_cash: Net cash = mapped cash $7.40B + short-term investments $8.37B - debt $7.08B = $8.70B (computed/valuation.json). Excluded on purpose: the $1.2B customer warrant liability (Q-14). It is equity-settled at $0.01, not settleable in cash (Q-13), and reclassified to Additional paid-in capital when tranches become exercisable. Its economic cost is captured by the full-dilution sensitivity in customer_warrants instead. Lease liabilities and long-term equity investments are also excluded as not material (unchanged from prior rounds).
